_why: THE UNIT-LEVEL DISAMBIGUATOR FOR DRAUGHTING, and it exists for one measured reason: NCO unit 3118 holds FOURTEEN draughting occupations and Batch 1 authors a role pack for exactly two of them. Bound to isco_unit_code '3118' at specificity 40, this pack catches the other twelve -- Draughtsperson Architectural / Civil / Electrical / Topographical / Structural, Plumbing Draftsman, Physical Design Engineer, Draftsman, Tracer, Blue Printer, Lithographic Designer, Draughtspersons Other -- while fam_cad_drafting sits above it at 50 on jd_nco_3118_0401 and jd_nco_3118_0402 and takes the mechanical pair. Without this family those twelve codes keep resolving to fam_universal@0: measured live this session, 'draftsman' -> jd_nco_3118_0301 -> fam_universal@0, which is a civil or electrical draughtsman getting eight trade-agnostic questions and no drawing question at all.
_structure: STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL TO fam_machining (unit 7223 @40) BENEATH fam_cnc_turning / fam_vmc_milling / fam_cnc_grinding (@50), and deliberately so -- that shape is proven by three role packs and needs no new engine behaviour. Most-specific-wins is the whole activation mechanism: a mechanical draughtsman lands on qp_cad_drafting, everyone else in the unit lands here, and nothing is special-cased anywhere in code. Two families may never claim the same target, so this pack owns unit 3118 alone.
_router_not_interview: THIS IS A ROUTER AND IT IS KEPT SHORT ON PURPOSE. Five items, 13 asks with the universal tail against a MAX_ENGINE_ASKS of 28. Its job is to (a) settle WHICH draughting line a worker is in, in his own words, and (b) capture the four facts that are true of every line -- software, drawing type, drawing work, workplace. Depth belongs in the role pack for a line once that line earns one; a civil-specific question here would be depth authored for a trade nobody has reviewed, which is the failure mode qp_machining avoids by asking machine_type and stopping. There is NO TIER GATE for the same reason: tiers exist to give a senior a different interview, and this pack does not claim to know what a senior architectural draughtsman should be asked.
_first_question: draughting_field IS THE DISAMBIGUATOR and is asked first, is_core + is_mandatory, exactly as machine_type is in qp_machining: retrieval pins the FAMILY, this settles which occupation within it. Its five real chips are the owner-decided split -- mechanical / civil / electrical / architectural / structural -- and the sixth is the escape a topographical draughtsman, tracer or blue printer needs so he is not forced to claim a line he does not work in. It routes to an ATTRIBUTE, not to rfs 'skills': a single_select writes one string, the skills field declares an array, and keepIfWellTyped REFUSES a chip whose value contradicts its field's declared type -- a chip the worker can tap with nothing recorded. An attribute has no declared type to contradict.
_shared_text: EVERY SERVED STRING HERE IS SHARED WITH A PACK THAT ALREADY HAS IT, which is the TTS point: audio is keyed by sha256(text) and shared across workers, so identical wording costs no new Devanagari twin. cad_software, drawing_type and drawing_work carry qp_cad_drafting's prompt and why_text verbatim; drawing_work's why_text is qp_vmc_milling's; workplace_type's prompt and why_text are qp_machining's, verbatim, and two of its labels with them. Only the OPTION SETS diverge, because a civil draughtsman's software is Revit and STAAD where a mechanical one's is SolidWorks -- and every dictionary that reads these attribute names is keyed by pack_id (R12 §2), so the divergence is expressible without a milling worker's answers being read through a turner's vocabulary.
review_note: DRAFTED, NOT RATIFIED. The draughting-line vocabulary here -- and the alias tranche that makes unit 3118 reachable at all -- is drafted for human ratification and has NOT yet been corrected by a practising draughtsman. See docs/registers/trade-content-ratification.md.
